NASB renders “authority” as “a right,” “a sister, a wife” as “a believing wife,” and “to take about” as “to take along.”
NASB follows the critical text; “permission” is rendered “a right,” and “not to work” is “to refrain from working.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the fruit”); “drink from the milk” is rendered “use the milk.”
NASB follows the critical text; “according to man” is rendered “according to human judgment,” and it casts the question as “am I?”
The quotation is in capitals; “treading out grain” is rendered “WHILE HE IS THRESHING,” and the question is cast as “is He?”
NASB follows the critical text; it adds “Yes” and “the crops.”
NASB renders “a great thing” as “too much.”
NASB renders “partake of” as “share” and “bear” as “endure.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “working the sacred things” as “perform sacred services” and “partake with” as “have their share with.”
NASB renders “prescribed” as “directed” and “to live from” as “to get their living from.”
NASB follows the critical text; it restructures the last clause as “than have any man make my boast an empty one.”
NASB follows the critical text; “necessity is laid upon me” is rendered “I am under compulsion.”
NASB renders “willingly” as “voluntarily” and “unwillingly” as “against my will.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of Christ”; “use up” is rendered “make full use of.”
NASB adds “though” and renders “servant” as “a slave” and “gain” as “win.”
NASB follows the critical text with “though not being myself under the Law.”
NASB follows the critical text; “outside the Law” is rendered “without law.”
NASB follows the critical text without “as”; it adds “men.”
NASB follows the critical text (“all things”).
NASB renders “grasp” as “win” and adds “only.”
NASB renders “striving” as “competes in the games,” “controls himself” as “exercises self-control,” and “crown” as “wreath.”
NASB renders “uncertainly” as “without aim” and “fight” as “box.”
NASB renders “batter” as “buffet” and “bring into servitude” as “make it my slave.”
